Freeport-McMoRan stock: $4.5 billion Bagdad expansion approved
sum: Freeport-McMoRan's board approved a $4.5 billion expansion and modernization program for the Bagdad copper and molybdenum operation in Arizona on Wednesday, November 4, the company said in a Freeport-McMoRan news release. The brownfield project is designed to more than double Bagdad's mining and milling rates and strengthen the miner's US copper growth strategy.

Freeport expects the mine to produce more than 400 million pounds of copper a year in the long term, including roughly 225 million pounds of incremental output. Molybdenum production is projected to exceed 20 million pounds annually, an increase of about 12 million pounds. Those figures describe planned output after the expansion rather than near-term production.

The project will add concentrator facilities with approximately 115,000 tons per day of incremental nameplate processing capacity. Supporting infrastructure includes a primary crusher, an overland conveyor, water and power systems, mining equipment and related facilities. Freeport said the plan will use Bagdad's existing infrastructure, reserve base and operating workforce.

Engineering, procurement planning and early works are under way. Construction is expected to take approximately three and a half years, with initial incremental production targeted for mid-2030. Freeport expects about 20 percent of project costs to be funded in 2027, 30 to 35 percent in 2028 and the balance in 2029 and 2030. The company said the spending will be incorporated into its updated capital expenditure outlook and treated as discretionary under its financial policy.

The company estimates a reduction of approximately 20 percent in long-term unit net cash costs. Management attributes the expected improvement to economies of scale, modern technology, automation and molybdenum by-product credits. The project economics are supported at a copper price of approximately $4.00 per pound and a molybdenum price of $20 per pound, according to the release.

Freeport said the expansion would make Bagdad the second-largest copper mine in the United States, behind its Morenci operation, and a leading US molybdenum producer. The mine has operated since 1945 and has a current reserve life exceeding 80 years before additional mineral resources are considered.

sum: Freeport-McMoRan reported stronger third-quarter earnings on October 27, 2026, as higher copper prices offset lower sales volumes during the recovery of its Grasberg operation in Indonesia. The Northern Miner reported that revenue rose 8% to 7.55 billion US dollars and net income attributable to common shareholders increased to 1.17 billion US dollars from 674 million US dollars a year earlier.

Freeport-McMoRan stock traded at 56.71 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 12:40 CET on Monday, November 2, 2026. The real-time quote of Freeport-McMoRan stock provides the latest trading reference for investors.

Adjusted earnings, which exclude 101 million US dollars in net charges, reached 88 cents per share and exceeded analyst expectations, according to The Northern Miner. Reported diluted earnings were 81 cents per share, compared with 46 cents in the third quarter of 2025.

The improvement came despite copper sales falling to 749 million pounds from 977 million pounds a year earlier. Freeport's realized copper price increased to 6.54 US dollars per pound from 4.68 US dollars, helping to offset the lower volumes. Quarterly copper production was 832 million pounds, with inventory accounting for part of the gap between production and sales.

Freeport reduced its consolidated copper-sales forecast to 3.0 billion pounds for 2026 from 3.1 billion pounds in its July forecast. The 2027 estimate fell to 3.7 billion pounds from 3.8 billion pounds, while the 2028 outlook remained 4.1 billion pounds. The company attributed the changes to lower operating rates in the United States and Chile and to updated mine plans.

The phased Grasberg restart remains the central driver of Freeport's volume outlook. The operation ran at 67% of capacity in the third quarter, up from earlier recovery levels, and mining rates at the Grasberg Block Cave averaged about 70,000 tonnes per day, compared with 53,000 tonnes in the second quarter.

Freeport expects Grasberg to reach 80% of capacity by mid-2027 and approach full capacity by the end of that year. Material-handling upgrades are scheduled for completion in early 2027, while preparations continue for a restart of Production Block 1S around mid-2027.

Changes in global manufacturing activity, supply availability, and demand patterns influence the broader metals sector and shape the environment in which copper producers operate.
